subsystems.name: Sample intake and fluidics
subsystems.role: takes in a few cubic centimetres of plume ice, brine or meltwater and moves it through the chip without contamination.

subsystems.name: Labelling reactor
subsystems.role: tags amino acids with a fluorescent dye so they can be seen at very low concentration.
parts: reaction channel held at controlled temperature

subsystems.name: Separation channel
subsystems.role: capillary electrophoresis that separates amino acids by charge and size, and resolves D from L enantiomers.
parts: background electrolyte and chiral selector (e.g. cyclodextrin)

subsystems.name: Fluorescence detector
subsystems.role: measures the light emitted by labelled molecules as they pass a point on the channel.
parts: laser diode or LED excitation source

subsystems.name: Control and data electronics
subsystems.role: runs the separation sequence and turns detector counts into a chromatogram.

subsystems.name: Chip substrate
subsystems.role: the physical platform that holds all channels, ports and electrodes in one bonded stack.

buildSteps.title: Design the channel layout
buildSteps.detail: A mask is drawn for the intake, reactor, injection cross and separation channel, sized so the separation length fits on a chip of a few centimetres.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the chip
buildSteps.detail: Channels tens of micrometres wide and deep are patterned by photolithography and etched or moulded into glass, fused silica or polymer.

buildSteps.title: Bond and integrate
buildSteps.detail: Layers are bonded to close the channels; fluidic ports, electrodes and a detection window are aligned and sealed.

buildSteps.title: Build the optics
buildSteps.detail: A laser or LED, filters and a photodetector are mounted and aligned to a fixed point on the separation channel.

buildSteps.title: Establish the chemistry
buildSteps.detail: Labelling reagent, buffer and a chiral selector are chosen and tested against standard mixtures of amino acids to confirm the reaction works inside a chip.

buildSteps.title: Validate chiral separation
buildSteps.detail: Mixtures of known D and L standards are run to show the enantiomers appear as separate peaks; detection limits and the smallest measurable enantiomeric excess are measured.

buildSteps.title: Harden for flight
buildSteps.detail: The instrument is shrunk and tested against vibration, thermal vacuum, radiation and autonomous operation, because no operator can intervene on a spacecraft.

buildSteps.title: Test on analogue samples
buildSteps.detail: The chip is run on terrestrial analogues such as glacier ice, sea ice brine and sulfate-rich spring deposits to prove it copes with real, messy samples.

prerequisites.tech: Chiral capillary electrophoresis and micellar electrokinetic chromatography
prerequisites.why: this is the only routine way to resolve D and L amino acids in tiny liquid volumes.
reagents such as fluorescamine or naphthalene-2,3-dicarboxaldehyde make amino acids detectable far below micromolar.
channels, pumps, valves and reaction zones must be merged onto one sealed device.
single-molecule-level fluorescence needs compact, low-power optics.
microfluidic capillary-electrophoresis instruments such as the JPL 'Chemical Laptop' have been demonstrated in the lab, but no wet-chemistry lab-on-a-chip has yet operated on a planetary mission.
Enceladus' plume was sampled and analysed remotely by Cassini, but collecting ice grains intact on a fast flyby and delivering them to a chip is not yet demonstrated.

pathway.milestone: bench prototypes separate amino acid standards and measure enantiomeric excess at sub-nanomolar levels
pathway.unlocks: proof that chiral analysis can be squeezed onto a chip.

pathway.milestone: integrated, automated instrument tested on ocean-world analogue ices and brines
pathway.unlocks: confidence that the chemistry survives real samples.

pathway.milestone: a flight-qualified package small enough to ride on a plume-flyby or lander mission
pathway.unlocks: in-situ chirality measurements rather than remote sensing.

pathway.milestone: analysis of plume material at Enceladus or Europa
pathway.unlocks: the first direct test for a non-racemic, potentially biological signature beyond Earth.
